notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order grouped by theme, not a chronology; surah order is not time order. The Companions of the Thicket are kept separate from the people of Madyan, as in the inventory; this file states only the ayat that name the Thicket.

chapters.title_en: The call to the Companions of the Thicket

claims.statement_en: The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.
Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God.
Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.
Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.
Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance.
Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land.
Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations.

chapters.summary_md: The Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers, and Shu'ayb called them to fear God and to obey him [c1][c2][c3]. He told them to give full measure, to weigh with the straight balance and not to spread corruption [c5][c6].
chapters.body_md: The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers [c1]. Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God [c2]. Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c3]. Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c4]. Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance [c5]. Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations [c7].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran says that the Companions of the Thicket denied the messengers (26:176) [c1].
- Shu'ayb said to them: will you not fear God (26:177) [c2].
- Shu'ayb told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:178-179) [c3].
- Shu'ayb told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:180) [c4].
- Shu'ayb told them to give full measure, not to be among those who cause loss, and to weigh with the straight balance (26:181-182) [c5].
- Shu'ayb told them not to diminish people's things and not to spread corruption in the land (26:183) [c6].
- Shu'ayb told them to fear Him who created them and the earlier creations (26:184) [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Shu'ayb spoke to the Companions of the Thicket [c2]. He told them to fear God [c3]. He told them to give full measure and not to take away from people what belonged to them [c5][c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The call joins fear of God with fairness in measure and weight [c3][c5]. One reading is that honest dealing appears here as part of what the messenger asks, together with a refusal of any wage [c4][c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the ayat of 26:177 name Shu'ayb but do not call him their brother, unlike other ayat that call a messenger their brother; the draft does not say whether this people is the same as another people.
- Not established: what the Thicket was, where it was, or how many Companions there were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any identification of the Thicket with a place, and any link to Madyan; none is used here.

claims.statement_en: They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars.
They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful.
Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did.
They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them.
The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day.
The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.
Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them.
A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions.

chapters.summary_md: The Companions of the Thicket called Shu'ayb a liar and told him to make a piece of the sky fall on them [c1][c2]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4].
chapters.body_md: They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars [c1]. They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful [c2]. Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did [c3]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them [c4]. The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day [c5]. The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers [c6]. Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them [c7]. A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions [c8].
chapters.deep_md:
- They told Shu'ayb that he was one of the bewitched, a human like them, and that they thought him one of the liars (26:177, 26:185-186) [c1].
- They told Shu'ayb to make a piece of the sky fall on them if he was truthful (26:187) [c2].
- Shu'ayb said that his Lord knew best what they did (26:188) [c3].
- They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow seized them (26:189) [c4].
- The ayah says that it was the punishment of a great day (26:189) [c5].
- The Quran says that in this there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers (26:190) [c6].
- Another passage says that the Companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers and that God took vengeance on them (15:78-79) [c7].
- A list of peoples names the Companions of the Thicket, with Thamud and the people of Lut, as the factions (38:13) [c8].
chapters.kids_md: The Companions of the Thicket did not believe Shu'ayb [c1]. They denied him, and the punishment of the day of the shadow came [c4]. The Quran says that this is a sign [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat set a challenge to bring down the sky beside Shu'ayb's reply that his Lord knows best [c2][c3]. One reading is that the reply leaves the judgement with God [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the day of the shadow was, or what is meant by the shadow; the ayah gives only the name.
- Not established: 15:79 ends with a dual pronoun whose referents are not named in the ayah; the draft does not use that part.
- Not established: whether the factions of 38:13 are the same peoples as the Companions of the Thicket; the draft states only that the list names them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: any link between the Companions of the Thicket and Madyan, and any date for the event.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Shu'ayb and the Companions of the Thicket. None is used in this draft.
Inventory refs: 50:14 (shared with the people of Tubba' and others) is not drafted here; it is used in the draft of Tubba'.
Wording a scholar should check first: 26:177 (named without the word brother), 26:185 (bewitched), 26:189 (the day of the shadow), 15:79 (the dual pronoun), 38:13 (factions).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the claim that the Companions of the Thicket and the people of Madyan are one people sent the same messenger; the draft keeps them apart.
